sat.topic: makers and fans who got more from AI this month

source.label: Your Instagram inspo sheet, with each story's own source

sat.copy: An animator, a filmmaker, game makers and football fans all got something from AI this month that millions chose to watch, play or hear. Each one credits the people behind it.
sat.hook: This month AI helped makers reach millions, and gave fans Motty back.

pitch.see: A gentleman with an umbrella helping New Yorkers, a painted Bible epic, a game world in brush strokes and a commentary box with John Motson's coat on the chair.
pitch.lands: It is uplifting, real and in the reader's world, and each story credits the human.
pitch.why_now: From 30 October to 26 November 2026; three found in your Instagram inspo sheet, one in the news this week.
pitch.share: Four makers, four tools, millions of viewers.

sat.funny: The AI did the frames; the human still had to decide the gentleman helps the pizza rat.

lookalike.our_take: The post rounded up the week's launches; ours rounds up the people who made something with them.

stories.headline: An animator's gentleman went viral helping New Yorkers
stories.what: "Englishman in New York" by @antrofrog follows an animated gentleman helping pedestrians, buskers and the pizza rat, made with Midjourney for the character and Seedance for the animation.
stories.why: One maker reached millions with a hand-drawn look and a kind character.

source.label: antrofrog on Instagram, Englishman in New York

stories.headline: A filmmaker turned classical paintings into a Bible epic
stories.what: "The Biblical Experience" by @samyazaspeaks moves through the Bible's best-known moments using classical paintings, camera moves and music.
stories.why: Centuries of religious art, brought to life by one filmmaker.

source.label: samyazaspeaks on Instagram, The Biblical Experience

stories.headline: Players built games and painted worlds in an afternoon
stories.what: People used a new Claude model to build playable games and 3D worlds in hours, including a game painted with about 1.5 million brush strokes a frame and a ride through Van Gogh's Starry Night.
stories.why: Making a game now starts with an idea, not a team.

source.label: evolving.ai on Instagram, games and worlds built with Claude Fable 5.2

stories.headline: Football fans can hear John Motson commentate again
stories.what: EA Sports FC 27 added an optional AI-recreated John Motson from 26 November, built from his original recordings with generative AI, with his widow's and son's permission; EA paid the family for the rights.
stories.why: A much-loved voice is back with consent and payment.

source.label: VGC, 25 Nov 2026
